Title: Netherlands – Ships and boats – 31199153: Bouw en levering 2 MPV-50 Vaartuigen
Procedure title: 31199153: Bouw en levering 2 MPV-50 Vaartuigen
Description: In het project MPV-50 (Multi Purpose Vessels) worden twee nieuwe vaartuigen gebouwd en geleverd, met als hoofdtaak markeren. Daarnaast zullen de vaartuigen worden ingezet bij incidentenbestrijding, meten ecologie, bevoorraden platforms en heeft de kustwacht een trekkingsrecht op de twee nieuwe vaartuigen. De vaartuigen zullen uitgerust worden met een duurzame energievoorziening, op basis van dual fuel methanol motoren en een batterijpakket. Met de ingebruikname van deze twee nieuwe vaartuigen worden de drie bestaande vaartuigen Rotterdam, Terschelling en Frans Naerebout vervangen. Binnen deze opdracht zal de opdrachtnemer de vaartuigen ontwerpen, bouwen en opleveren. Zie korte beschrijving.

{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":183853,"idEra":24774,"activityNumber":"1000045894","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-13360","title":"T811-900GS OPTIMIZATION OF LASER INTENSITY ON SPACE DEBRIS VIA COHERENT BEAM COMBINATION (EXPRO+)","description":"Recently, strategies have been explored to perturb space debris orbits using high-power ground-based lasersystems. This method, known as laser momentum transfer, can also be used for deep-space opticalcommunications. Multi-beam architectures have been designed and implemented to obtain the required powerlevels that would be unachievable with a single laser source or that would be limited by atmospheric turbulenceeffects. In a recent study on laser momentum transfer, 40 kW-class lasers based on multiple beams have beenproposed to alter the orbits of space debris and prevent collisions with active satellites.One challenge is delivering the generated power to the selected target while minimizing losses caused by laserpropagation and ensuring efficient momentum transfer for collision avoidance manoeuvres. Adaptive opticssystems have been considered but there are still several challenges due to the limited maturity of thistechnology. For example, retrieving tip-tilt information to compensate for atmospheric turbulence still dependson sunlight reflected from debris, which is a limiting factor in operational terms. Additionally, today's deformablemirror technology is not mature enough for the power levels needed for this application.
